newsitem.title: USA: Federal-Mogul trims 1996 outlook, chairman resigns.
newsitem.headline: Federal-Mogul trims 1996 outlook, chairman resigns.

text.p: Federal-Mogul Corp on Wednesday lowered expectations for 1996 financial results and said Dennis Gormley is resigning as chairman and chief executive.

"While we expect the company's operating performance for 1996 to exceed 1995 results, we do not expect to achieve our previously forecasted earnings level for 1996 or the level that analysts are anticipating," said Robert Miller, a board member who will be chairman of the executive committee and acting CEO during the search for a new chief.
Shares in the company on Wednesday were up 5/8 to 19-3/8.
Gormley, 56, underwent successful coronary artery bypass surgery on August 20.
The company declined to detail reasons for Gormley's resignation.
The maker and distributor of parts for autos, trucks, and farm and construction vehicles said it hired Korn/Ferry International to assist in a search for a new CEO.

The company reported net earnings on an operating basis in 1995 of $40.8 million, or $0.92 per share, excluding a fourth-quarter $42-million special charge on accounting changes, sales of assets and restructuring.
Federal-Mogul said earlier this year that 1996 earnings would be 50 percent above those of 1995. Analysts had been forecasting 1996 earnings of about $1.25 per share.
